newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar settles weaker but off lows.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar settles weaker but off lows.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures ended a volatile session weaker, but local shortcovering and light trade buying during the second half of the session lifted the market off the lows made early, dealers said.

Early speculative buying carried the benchmark July contract over resistance at 11.20 cents a lb and to a high of 11.21 cents, where the buying dried up. The lack of interest prompted locals selling, which which knocked July toward 11.00 cents.
Sell stops pressured the contract to the low of 10.94 cents, traders said.
"It was like a vacuum. There was nothing under the market and prices came off very quickly," a floor source said.
The most-active month settled down 0.09 at 11.06 cents after trading from 11.21 to 10.94 cents. The outer months closed 0.05 and 0.02 lower.

July's close over 11.05 cents was viewed as positive, but traders said the speculators, who have fueled recent gains, are unlikely to continue their buying spree in the face of a heavy net long position and a dearth of physical offtake.
Open interest in the July contract rose by 1,617 lots to 74,657 lots, as of early Wednesday. October's open interest climbed 1,456 lots to 42,745 lots.
Trade selling above 11.20 cents in July, and on a scale-up basis in October, will also keep a lid on further gains, floor sources added.
"It's a question of who will out-last who," a dealer said. "I doubt the specs are in a position to add more."
Traders pegged major support at 10.70 cents in July. They said activity should remain rangebound on Friday, ahead of the long Memorial Day weekend.
An estimated 21,839 lots changed hands on the day, compared with Wednesday's official 20,182 lots.
